.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A coastal low will develop off the Florida coast late this 
week and will pass through the local area Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A coastal low will develop off the Florida 
coast late this week and will pass through the local area Sunday
into Monday.

High pressure over the Mid-Atlantic area will move offshore by 
Saturday. Meanwhile, surface low pressure will develop and 
organize east of the Florida coast late this week and will track
along the coast this weekend. Conditions remain dry over the 
local area through Saturday, and then there is uncertainty as to
the exact track and strength of that low.

The 12Z/18 operational GFS is closer to the coast and weaker 
compared to the 12Z/18 AIGFS, which has much more rainfall over 
eastern Delaware and New Jersey. The 12Z/18 operational ECMWF 
actually has a secondary low spin off ahead of the primary low, 
and then the primary low passes well east of the New Jersey 
coast on Monday and Monday night. The 12Z/18 EC-AIFS is similar 
to the AIGFS in that it is just off the New Jersey coast and has
widespread heavy rain a bit farther west, across New Jersey and
just west of the I-95 corridor. There is still plenty of time 
for the detail to sort themselves out, but the highest PoPs look
to be at least Sunday and Sunday night. PoPs on Sunday are up 
to 60 percent for most of Delmarva and most of New Jersey and 40
to 50 percent for southeast Pennsylvania and northern New 
Jersey. The national Hurricane Center has a 40 percent chance 
for cyclone formation in the next 7 days over the western 
Atlantic Ocean.

A strong cold front follows through Monday night and cold air 
returns for the new week.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
The following discussion is for KPHL, KPNE, KTTN, KABE, KRDG, 
KILG, KMIV, KACY and surrounding areas. 

Tonight...Mainly VFR/SKC. Some patchy fog is possible again
after 09Z, especially in the same areas that experienced fog
last night. Opted to include some MVFR restrictions for RDG,
ABE, and MIV. Westerly winds less than 5 kts to calm. High 
confidence in prevailing conditions.

Thursday...VFR/SKC. Light west to northwest winds early shifting
southwesterly between 15-18Z near 5 kts. High confidence.

Outlook...

Thursday night through Saturday...VFR. No significant weather.

Sunday and Monday...Restrictions in rain and low clouds 
becoming likely. There is potential for gusty winds.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine headlines through Thursday as high pressure continues
to bring lighter winds and seas at or below 2 feet.

Outlook...

Thursday night through Saturday...No marine headlines are 
anticipated.

Sunday and Monday...At least Small Craft Advisory conditions 
becoming likely along with increasing seas due to a coastal 
storm.
